text:
anya: FYI I'm seeing 'ghost' insertions during a live hot-reload that only happen after ~48k tokens on 3-shard configs. Not the usual off-by-one; the stream inserts unrelated tokens and later recovers.

raj: do you have a tiny repro we can run in CI? sounds like a pos-base vs local-index handshake bug on reshard/hotstart.

anya: yes - repro command below. It reliably hits after ~47.8k tokens when we call the hot-reload endpoint.
```
./serve --model atlas30b --shards 3 --context 98304 --quant int4 --batch 1 --streaming \
  --hot-reload-url http://localhost:8080/admin/hot-reload
# trigger: curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/admin/hot-reload -d '{"quant":"int3"}'
```

sasha: can you paste the excerpt from the stream where it diverges? short token id diff is fine.

anya: sure. here's token ids around the insertion point (global positions included):
```
pos: 47892 47893 47894 47895 47896 47897 47898
expected: ... 221 19 444 7 88 330 900
actual:   ... 221 19 444 7 88 1221 330
# note: token 900 replaced by 1221 at pos 47897, then sequence realigns at 47898
```

raj: that pattern (single unexpected token then realign) smells like a race where one shard advances its local_pos_base while others still use the old base during a write to the shared kv ring. Could be off by a stride when remapping local_index in the hot-reload path.

anya: I dumped the per-shard metadata before and after reload with `tools/kv_meta_dump` - after reload shard 2 shows local_pos_base=47880 while shards 0/1 show 47896. The write for global pos 47897 landed in the wrong slot on shard 2 and created a transient alias.

sasha: paste the dump snippet?

anya: pasted below (trimmed):
```
# /tmp/kv-meta-shard2.json (after reload)
{"shard":2, "local_pos_base": 47880, "stride": 16, "epoch": 42}
# /tmp/kv-meta-shard0.json
{"shard":0, "local_pos_base": 47896, "stride": 16, "epoch": 42}
```

raj: aha, epoch matches but pos_base mismatch. That explains the transient alias. Which code path sets local_pos_base during the hot-reload? I remember commit f3a9b2d touched the hotstart handshake.

anya: hot-reload calls `reshard::remap_local_index()` then `kv::swap_quant_table()` in parallel. If remap finishes later on one shard you get the mismatch. We probably need a barrier so that remap and metadata commit is atomic across shards.

sasha: good catch. Could also add a sanity check in the write path that rejects writes if the global_pos < local_pos_base or > local_pos_base + capacity. Fail-fast would surface the issue instead of stealthy ghost tokens.

ci-bot: regression job 6123 flaked on eng-ml/longsession-hot-reload  ticket: https://redwood.internal/bugs/6123

raj: plan: (1) quick guard in the kv write path to assert local_pos_base is within range and log + drop write if not, (2) add a global-barrier in hot-reload to commit pos_base change synchronously, (3) add integration test that triggers hot-reload while streaming 100k tokens across 3 shards.

anya: assigned to raj for the guard+test. I'll draft the barrier change and open a PR with dumps and the failing CI job attached.

sasha: add a randomized long prompt (diverse tokens) to the integration so token collisions will reveal aliasing, not just repeated sequences. Also record rot-phase checks in the test logs.

raj: starting a small patch now: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/4422 (WIP) - includes a KV write guard and a diagnostic that emits mismatch reasons.

anya: thanks. once PR is up, can we run it on a Dedicated nightly image? have a customer running 3-shard longsession this week.

ci-bot: nightly-deploy 2026-03-22 queued - include PR 4422 in canary run.

anya: cheers. if the guard reduces silent data mutations, we can backfill a smoke test that scans recent longsession logs for 'ghost insertion' patterns and alert. :eyes:
